# FlashAlpha.Historical .NET SDK

> Official .NET / C# client for the **FlashAlpha Historical API** —
> point-in-time replay of every live options-analytics endpoint
> (GEX, gamma flip, VRP, narrative, max pain, 0DTE, full stock
> summary, exposure levels) at any minute back to 2017-01-03.

Same response shapes as the live FlashAlpha API — just pass an `at`
timestamp to ask "what did dealer positioning look like at 14:30 ET on
2020-03-16?". Backtest options strategies against 80B+ option rows.

- Package: `dotnet add package FlashAlpha.Historical`
- Target: .NET 8.0+
- Auth: same `X-Api-Key` you use for `api.flashalpha.com`
- Playground: <https://lab.flashalpha.com/swagger>
- API project URL: <https://historical.flashalpha.com>

## What this SDK provides

- `FlashAlphaHistoricalClient` — typed, async, `IDisposable` HTTP wrapper.
  Every analytics method takes a required `at` parameter (string or
  `DateTime`).
- `Backtester` and `Replay` — high-level helpers for iterating across
  daily / minute-resolution timestamps and running a callback per step.
- Typed response POCOs under `FlashAlpha.Historical.Models` — same field
  names as the live SDK so you can swap clients without changing consumer
  code.

## Sister package

`FlashAlpha` (separate NuGet) is the live variant — drop the `at=`
parameter and you have real-time analytics. The two SDKs use deliberately
identical POCO shapes.

## Endpoints (selected highlights)

| Endpoint | SDK method |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/stock/{symbol}/summary?at=...` | `StockSummaryAsync` |
| `GET /v1/exposure/gex/{symbol}?at=...` | `GexAsync` |
| `GET /v1/exposure/levels/{symbol}?at=...` | `ExposureLevelsAsync` |
| `GET /v1/exposure/summary/{symbol}?at=...` | `ExposureSummaryAsync` |
| `GET /v1/exposure/narrative/{symbol}?at=...` | `NarrativeAsync` |
| `GET /v1/exposure/zero-dte/{symbol}?at=...` | `ZeroDteAsync` |
| `GET /v1/maxpain/{symbol}?at=...` | `MaxPainAsync` |
| `GET /v1/vrp/{symbol}?at=...` | `VrpAsync` |
| `GET /v1/stockquote/{symbol}?at=...` | `StockQuoteAsync` |
| `GET /v1/optionquote/{symbol}?at=...` | `OptionQuoteAsync` |
| `GET /v1/surface/{symbol}?at=...` | `SurfaceAsync` |

The `at` parameter accepts:
- `"2026-03-05T15:30:00"` (full ISO timestamp, ET assumed)
- `"2026-03-05"` (defaults to 16:00 ET)
- `DateTime` overload

## Data provenance

Every response carries two objects in the same shape. `archive_as_of` is the vintage of
the archive rows actually replayed for the timestamp requested - equity and index spot,
their option chains, futures and futures options, the classified trade tape, settled open
interest, and the macro series, each reported separately because they are stored and
replayed independently. `data_as_of` is the live-feed counterpart and reports `null` for every feed here,
because a replay node reads the archive and consumes no live feed; it is still returned so
the envelope has one shape across the live and historical services, and so a historical
response cannot be mistaken for a live one. `endpoint_version` identifies the deployment.

`archive_as_of` is what makes an archive gap detectable. Request a moment with no row and
the query returns the most recent earlier row; nothing else in the response distinguishes
the two. Point-in-time work should read it and drop or flag observations whose inputs
precede the requested instant by more than the study tolerates. `oi_feed` trailing by a
session is correct rather than a gap: settled open interest is published once per session,
so the newest figure that existed at any intraday moment is the prior close. Every response
model inherits `FlashAlphaResponse`, so all three are typed members. Full reference:
https://flashalpha.com/docs/lab-api-overview#response-envelope

## Typed response models

POCOs live under `FlashAlpha.Historical.Models` (`StockSummaryResponse`,
`ExposureSummaryResponse`, `ExposureLevelsResponse`, `NarrativeResponse`,
`MaxPainResponse`, `VrpResponse`, `ZeroDteResponse`). Field names and
nullability mirror the live API.

`AsOf` on every typed response is the timestamp the API actually used —
**snapped to the available minute**, may not equal the `at` you requested.

## Tier breakdown

The Historical API requires the **Alpha plan or higher** on every
endpoint. Sign up: <https://flashalpha.com>.

## Quick start

```csharp
using FlashAlpha.Historical;

using var hx = new FlashAlphaHistoricalClient("YOUR_API_KEY");

// What did dealer positioning look like during the COVID crash?
var snap = await hx.ExposureSummaryAsync("SPY", "2020-03-16T15:30:00");
Console.WriteLine(snap.GetProperty("regime").GetString());
// → "negative_gamma"
```

### Daily replay

```csharp
using FlashAlpha.Historical;

using var hx = new FlashAlphaHistoricalClient("YOUR_API_KEY");
var bt = new Backtester(hx, Backtester.StockSummaryEndpoint, "SPY");

var results = await bt.RunAsync(
    Replay.IterDays(new(2024, 1, 2), new(2024, 3, 29)),
    (at, snap) => new
    {
        Vrp = snap.GetProperty("volatility").GetProperty("vrp").GetDouble(),
        Regime = snap.GetProperty("exposure").GetProperty("regime").GetString(),
    });
```

### Minute-resolution replay

```csharp
await foreach (var step in Replay.RunAsync(
    hx, Backtester.ExposureSummaryEndpoint, "SPY",
    Replay.IterMinutes(new(2025, 1, 15), new(2025, 1, 15), stepMinutes: 15)))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{step.At} {step.Response.GetProperty("regime").GetString()}");
}
```
